parallel.requirements: Recognized the C++ test10 program, glibc-style atoi behavior, trailing-space output, pure std Rust, Cargo project, and black-box implementation constraint.
parallel.plan_and_ownership: The parent owned implementation and local testing, created task trackers, then delegated broad verifier/auditor/oracle work to a workflow with many child agents.
parallel.implementation: Implemented Cargo.toml, test10.rs, and mapbox earcut modules; compiled with rustc and cargo and performed differential and property checks before workflow completion.
parallel.integration_and_delivery: Integrated the final source tree under /output and produced test10 plus Cargo artifacts; artifact validation copied the expected deliverable despite process timeout.
parallel.verification: Ran local byte-for-byte and property checks, then launched a large workflow whose partial child results found and investigated edge cases but never synthesized.
parallel.unfinished_or_incorrect: The final response is empty and workflow result is null because the process timed out; official evaluation nevertheless passed all 37 cases.

serial.requirements: Recognized the same prompt obligations: Rust 2021, byte-identical CLI/output, no crates, Cargo project, black-box use of the C++ executable.
serial.plan_and_ownership: Used one local trajectory with no workflows or subagents; the same actor owned implementation, integration, tests, build, and final report.
serial.implementation: Implemented a Cargo project with test10.rs and earcut modules, including node, geometry, z-order, and validation tests.
serial.integration_and_delivery: Built the executable and release binary in /output with a coherent final tree accepted by artifact validation.
serial.verification: Reported byte-for-byte comparisons, coordinate bit parity, cargo tests, rustc/cargo builds, no external dependencies, and official evaluation passed.
serial.unfinished_or_incorrect: No unfinished serial workflow or implementation work is visible; serial closed normally with a final summary.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel recognized the source program, examples, Rust 2021, CLI parsing, byte-identical output, std-only, Cargo structure, and black-box library requirement.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial received the same prompt and implemented the same pure-Rust, byte-identical CLI and output obligations.
comparison_dimensions.difference: No requirement coverage difference affected the official outcome; both ultimately satisfied the current evaluator.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel split work into parent-owned implementation tasks and a workflow-owned verification fan-out with differential, audit, oracle, verifier, and synthesis phases.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial kept implementation and verification in one trajectory with workflows disabled and no delegated child logs.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel had broad verification ownership distributed across many children; serial had a single local owner for the full pipeline.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel children received a detailed shared workflow context describing the C++ behavior, the /output Rust port, build command, audit rules, and no-write scratch policy.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial did not need inter-agent interfaces; the same task context stayed inside one actor through implementation and final verification.
comparison_dimensions.difference: The main context was preserved well enough for child audits; the adverse issue was not missing requirements or interface mismatch.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel wrote a Cargo project, mapbox modules, a large earcut implementation, and test10.rs, then rebuilt and differentially tested the output.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial wrote a Cargo project with earcut modules, test10.rs, a tests module, and verified the artifact before finalizing.
comparison_dimensions.difference: The two ports used different module naming and validation breadth, but both produced acceptable artifacts.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel launched the workflow, received some child results in the journal, then the workflow was killed with null aggregate result and no final response.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial completed its local result lifecycle, emitted a final response, and had no workflow or delegation join to wait for.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel lost the workflow synthesis stage to timeout; serial closed cleanly without any child result lifecycle.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel parent wrote the implementation workspace and told verifier children not to modify /output, while artifact validation later found a coherent deliverable.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial integrated locally and artifact validation copied the expected Cargo files, binary, and source modules.
comparison_dimensions.difference: No concrete shared-state collision or overwrite explains a behavioral difference; both artifacts validated.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel performed local differential tests and property checks, then started a much broader child verification workflow that did not synthesize before timeout; the official retry passed 37/37.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial reported byte-for-byte comparisons, coordinate parity, unit tests, final builds, and the current official evaluation passed 37/37.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel had more concurrent verification breadth but less closure; serial had narrower but completed verification and final reporting.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel exhausted the run window with return code 143 after 2399 seconds, one workflow, twenty child logs, and nearly one million child tokens.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial returned code 0 after 843 seconds with workflow tools disabled and zero workflow tasks.
comparison_dimensions.difference: The adverse process difference is closure: parallel spent the remaining budget on fan-out verification, while serial finalized normally.

outcome_analysis.explanation: There is no current official outcome discordance: both current status.json evaluation records are completed and passed 37/37. The parallel trajectory differs materially in process, because a successful artifact was followed by a broad verification workflow that was killed before final synthesis, whereas the serial trajectory completed local verification and final response normally. The stale parallel evaluation summary shows an incomplete failed evaluator attempt, but status.json records the successful official retry and controls the outcome.
parallel_contributors: Completed a working artifact before the broad verification workflow exhausted closure budget.
Used extensive workflow verification that added process cost and left final synthesis unfinished.
serial_contributors: Kept implementation and verification local with workflows disabled.
Finished normally and reported completed byte-for-byte and unit-test verification.
ordinary_implementation_differences: Parallel and serial used different internal module layouts and different supplemental verification breadth, but neither difference changed the official pass outcome.
evaluator_effects: Parallel cell/evaluation/summary.json is stale and incomplete; the current completed cell/status.json evaluation supersedes it.
outcome_analysis.causal_scope: no outcome difference; retained pattern is an adverse parallel process consequence only

The parent explicitly owned implementation, build, local verification, workflow launch, and final artifact path; the pipeline was delayed, not ownerless.
Implementation was not blocked behind one serial preflight; the parent wrote the port before broad verification fan-out.
Investigation and verification were not a first serial phase that deferred implementation; productive implementation preceded and overlapped later verification.
The better-supported boundary is broad collective fan-out exhausting the budget, not auxiliary work starving a separately identifiable critical implementation path.
The workflow fanned fourteen work items into child agents and verifier sub-agents; retries and live children consumed the remaining budget before aggregate result or final synthesis.
candidates.realized_consequence: Workflow verification consumed the remaining run window, was killed with null aggregate result, and prevented a final synthesis even though the artifact later passed.
candidates.near_match_reason: The unreturned verifier synthesis is downstream of the same killed fan-out episode, not a separate completed verifier finding trapped below the parent.

candidates.reason: No single child scope is the causal boundary; the adverse event comes from collective breadth and nested verifier spawning across the workflow.
The workflow context included task behavior, output, CLI, no dependency, build, and no-write requirements; child incompletion followed fan-out budget pressure, not a missing brief.
Children audited a shared completed port rather than producing separately integrated components, so no omitted interoperation contract caused incompatible work.
No known requirement or finding is shown lost through transfer; the workflow state retained child results and progress records.
Returned child reports were not shown to be available but too bulky for the parent to reduce; the parent process timed out before aggregate workflow return.
No receiver acted on superseded workspace or requirement state; child briefs targeted the current /output port.
Some child findings differed, but no parent decision point adjudicated incompatible handoffs; the workflow never reached synthesis because it was killed.
The parallel parent did not present a whole-task completion decision after the workflow; the final file is empty and official status, not parent acceptance, establishes pass.
Workflow retries followed stall detection but there is no completed replacement that repeated prior work without usable checkpoint as the distinct adverse boundary.

candidates.reason: Children and workflow were killed as the run ended; this is downstream of fan-out budget exhaustion rather than an independent explicit early stop boundary.
A usable artifact was already built and officially passed; the missing piece was workflow synthesis/final response, not promotion of an unplaced deliverable.
No evidence shows a child implementation was merged after integrated verification without rechecking.
Children were verifier/auditor agents, not owners of completed implementation patches that the parent failed to retrieve or integrate.
The absent verifier aggregate is the terminal effect of killed fan-out with null workflow result, not a separate completed verifier finding trapped below the parent.
The unfinished child scopes were verifier/audit work after the artifact was complete; lack of takeover is the same timeout chain, not a separate required implementation failure.
The parent did not receive a final workflow bundle and then proceed inconsistently with it; available child results remained inside a killed workflow.
The parent did inspect workflow progress and journal state while waiting; the realized issue is breadth consuming budget, not absence of inspection.
Verifier children were instructed to use /tmp and not modify /output; no competing implementation designs required reconciliation.
No two live agents edited the same source file with one observing or reconciling another live edit.
No child replaced parent-owned library or configuration source; verifier work stayed in scratch directories.
No concurrent actor overwrote the required test10 entry point or executable while another owned or used it.
No broad cleanup, rebuild, or promotion invalidated another agent's final-tree work.
Although agents shared read access to /output, the workflow required scratch work and no concrete unstable provenance problem is shown.
No generated fixture, cache, temporary path, or auxiliary artifact from one concurrent actor was consumed as stable input by another.

retained_patterns.reason: The workflow expanded the completed-port verification into fourteen child work items and nested verifier agents; the workflow state records twenty agents, null result, killed status, and 944266 child tokens, while the parent timed out before final synthesis.
retained_patterns.realized_consequence: The verification workflow consumed the remaining run window and was killed before returning an aggregate result or final synthesis; the parallel final response remained empty.
retained_patterns.near_match_reason: The missing verifier return is not independent because correcting the fan-out budget episode would also resolve the absent aggregate result.

suppressed_same_chain_candidates: Critical-Path Starvation, Oversized Child Task, Early Child Termination, Missing Verifier Return, No Failure Takeover, and Blind Timeout Wait are all downstream descriptions of the same killed verification fan-out chain, not independent episodes.
